scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too hard on my boyfriend or if he's overreacting. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a long day, and I can imagine how exhausting that must be. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. That seems like a good setup for maintaining a relationship without the constant stress of living together. Now, my son decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's 12 years old and really excited about it. Initially, I thought about asking my boyfriend to pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom, she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. Even though he's been in my life for three years, she made it clear that I should handle it. So, I ended up paying for it, but to afford it, I had to extend my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, whereas we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. He got really angry and told me that he had to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I wasn't home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. He then suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. I was like, "Really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world, love!" The little sneak then went over to see my mom and had a heart-to-heart with her, which ended up in her calling me and telling me I'm out of line. Now, I'm wondering who is in the right here. Is it me being too demanding, or is my boyfriend overreacting? Okay, so I need to break this down. First, the responsibility of paying for my son's football. My mom made it clear that it's my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. But he's been in my life for three years, so does that mean he should contribute to my son's activities? Or is it solely my responsibility as the parent? Then, the issue of picking up and dropping off my son on weekends. My boyfriend works long hours, and I can understand that he wants to have some downtime on weekends. But I had to extend my work hours to afford the football, so I'm already stretched thin. Asking him to help with the logistics seems reasonable, but he felt it was too much to ask. He also mentioned that he wants to use his weekends to go to football games since I'm not home anyway. That seems like a valid point. He has his own life and interests, and he deserves time to relax and enjoy his weekends. But I snapped at him and made him feel guilty for not wanting to help, which probably escalated the situation. Then, when my son went to my mom and she told me I'm out of line, that adds another layer of complexity. It seems like my mom is taking his side, which is making me feel even more isolated. So, is it right or wrong for me to ask my boyfriend to help with these responsibilities? On one hand, he's been in my life for a long time, and it's reasonable to expect some level of support, especially since he's involved in my son's life. On the other hand, he has his own responsibilities and needs to have a life outside of our relationship. Maybe the issue is more about communication and setting expectations early on. If I had discussed these responsibilities earlier, maybe he wouldn't feel so overwhelmed now. But since I only brought it up when I needed help, it came off as demanding. Also, the fact that my mom is expecting me to handle everything on my own might be influencing my expectations. It's possible that I'm used to handling things independently, and now I'm trying to involve my boyfriend in a way that he's not comfortable with. In the end, he suggested breaking up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. That seems extreme, but I can see how feeling overwhelmed and undervalued could lead to that reaction. It's important to have a balanced relationship where both partners feel they're contributing and being supported. So, maybe I need to reflect on how I approached the situation and whether I could have communicated my needs in a way that was less demanding. At the same time, I should consider his needs and boundaries to ensure that the relationship remains healthy and balanced. Overall, it's a tough situation, and there's no clear right or wrong. It's more about finding a middle ground where both partners feel respected and supported.
